q: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities, that have only magnitude, are called ____.
e: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities, that have only magnitude, are called scalar quantities. Scalar quantities here means a quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

q: However, some quantities have a directional quality. Not only the magnitude but also the direction is required for the complete description of such quantities. These quantities, that have both magnitude and direction, are called ____.
e: However, some quantities have a directional quality. Not only the magnitude but also the direction is required for the complete description of such quantities. These quantities, that have both magnitude and direction, are called vectors. The physics in this sentence is built around vectors.

q: In printing, vectors are represented by boldface type, such as A, F, v, s. In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing ____ on the top of their symbols.
e: In printing, vectors are represented by boldface type, such as A, F, v, s. In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing arrows on the top of their symbols. The physics in this sentence is built around arrows.

q: The magnitude of F is written as ____.
e: The magnitude of F is written as F = |F|. The physics in this sentence is built around F = |F|.

q: A = B: A and B are equal in magnitude and have the ____.
e: A = B: A and B are equal in magnitude and have the same direction. Same direction here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: A = -B: A and B are equal in magnitude but have ____.
e: A = -B: A and B are equal in magnitude but have opposite directions. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite directions.

q: A = 2B: The magnitude of A is two times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is the ____ as that of B.
e: A = 2B: The magnitude of A is two times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is the same as that of B. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: A = -3B: The magnitude of A is three times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is ____ to that of B.
e: A = -3B: The magnitude of A is three times the magnitude of B and the direction of A is opposite to that of B. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite.

q: Using graphical method a vector may be represented by an ____. The length of the arrow is proportional to the magnitude of the vector and the direction of the arrow gives the direction of the vector.
e: Using graphical method a vector may be represented by an arrow. The length of the arrow is proportional to the magnitude of the vector and the direction of the arrow gives the direction of the vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: To add A and B, first draw A. Then draw B in such a way that the tail of B is at the tip of A. Then draw a third vector R from the tail of A to the tip of B. R is the vector sum A + B and it is called the ____.
e: To add A and B, first draw A. Then draw B in such a way that the tail of B is at the tip of A. Then draw a third vector R from the tail of A to the tip of B. R is the vector sum A + B and it is called the resultant vector.

q: A + B = B + A. Vector addition is ____.
e: A + B = B + A. Vector addition is commutative. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: In algebraic notation, A − B = A + (−B). Hence, vector subtraction is not ____.
e: In algebraic notation, A − B = A + (−B). Hence, vector subtraction is not commutative. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called ____ of a vector, and the new vectors obtained are called vector components of the original vector.
e: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called resolution of a vector, and the new vectors obtained are called vector components of the original vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two ____ components, namely, horizontal component and vertical component.
e: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two perpendicular components, namely, horizontal component and vertical component. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ.
e: A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ. The physics in this sentence is built around $A_x = A \cos \theta$, $A_y = A \sin \theta$.

q: Distance (or) distance travelled by the body is the length of the path along which the body ____.
e: Distance (or) distance travelled by the body is the length of the path along which the body moves. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

q: The displacement of the body is a vector directed from the starting point to the ____.
e: The displacement of the body is a vector directed from the starting point to the end point. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Displacement is the distance travelled along a ____.
e: Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a ____.
e: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a scalar. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

q: Displacement has a specific direction. It is always directed from the starting point to the end point. It has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a ____.
e: Displacement has a specific direction. It is always directed from the starting point to the end point. It has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a vector. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: The average speed, v_av (or) v̄, is the ratio of total distance s to ____.
e: The average speed, v_av (or) v̄, is the ratio of total distance s to time taken t. Time taken t here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force.

q: The average velocity, v_av (or) v̄, is the ratio of total displacement s to ____.
e: The average velocity, v_av (or) v̄, is the ratio of total displacement s to time taken t. Time taken t here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is ____.
e: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is zero. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends. Velocity is directed.

q: The speed and velocity which represent a motion for a certain period of time interval are called average speed and average velocity, whereas, the speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as ____ and instantaneous velocity.
e: The speed and velocity which represent a motion for a certain period of time interval are called average speed and average velocity, whereas, the speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as instantaneous speed and instantaneous velocity. Instantaneous speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Note that the speedometer of a car indicates the ____ of the car.
e: Note that the speedometer of a car indicates the instantaneous speed of the car. Instantaneous speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Instantaneous speed v = lim_(Δt→0) Δs/Δt.
e: Instantaneous speed v = lim_(Δt→0) Δs/Δt. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Instantaneous velocity v = lim_(Δt→0) Δs⃗/Δt.
e: Instantaneous velocity v = lim_(Δt→0) Δs⃗/Δt. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of ____.
e: The instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of distance. Distance here means the path length travelled, with no direction. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: The instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of ____.
e: The instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of displacement. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain ____.
e: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Motion with constant velocity is known as ____.
e: Motion with constant velocity is known as uniform motion. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an ____.
e: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an acceleration. Acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Motion with changing velocity is called non-uniform motion (or) ____.
e: Motion with changing velocity is called non-uniform motion (or) accelerated motion. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity. Acceleration is not velocity.

q: The average acceleration a_c is defined by the equation, a = (v − v₀)/____.
e: The average acceleration a_c is defined by the equation, a = (v − v₀)/t. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Instantaneous acceleration a = lim_(Δt→0) Δv/Δt = ____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration a = lim_(Δt→0) Δv/Δt = $\frac{dv}{dt}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of ____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is increasing and negative if the magnitude of velocity is ____.
e: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is increasing and negative if the magnitude of velocity is decreasing. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity. Acceleration is not velocity.

q: Negative acceleration is usually called ____ or retardation.
e: Negative acceleration is usually called deceleration or retardation. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Motion along a straight line is called ____.
e: Motion along a straight line is called linear motion. Linear motion names motion along a straight line.

q: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is equal to the ____.
e: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is equal to the distance moved. Distance moved here means the path length travelled, with no direction. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The magnitude of the velocity is also equal to the ____.
e: The magnitude of the velocity is also equal to the speed. Speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The most simplest type of motion is the linear motion with constant velocity (____).
e: The most simplest type of motion is the linear motion with constant velocity (uniform motion). Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Since the velocity is constant, the acceleration is ____.
e: Since the velocity is constant, the acceleration is zero. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity. Acceleration is not velocity.

q: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the ____.
e: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the same. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is v = ____.
e: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is v = $\frac{s}{t}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, i.e., the velocity of a body changes at a constant rate, then the acceleration is said to be ____.
e: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, i.e., the velocity of a body changes at a constant rate, then the acceleration is said to be constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Since the acceleration is constant, the instantaneous acceleration and average acceleration are the ____.
e: Since the acceleration is constant, the instantaneous acceleration and average acceleration are the same. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: v = v₀ + ____.
e: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: v = v₀ + $at$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: v² = v₀² + ____.
e: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: v² = v₀² + $2as$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: s = v₀t + ____.
e: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: s = v₀t + $\frac{1}{2}at^2$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: s = ____.
e: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: s = $\bar{v}t$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: $\bar{v}$ = ____.
e: The equations of motion for constant acceleration are: $\bar{v}$ = $\frac{v_0 + v}{2}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In describing the equations of motion we shall not use the vector notation, i.e., we will omit the arrows on the symbols as the direction of motion is already ____.
e: In describing the equations of motion we shall not use the vector notation, i.e., we will omit the arrows on the symbols as the direction of motion is already fixed. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: However, we will use positive (+) and negative (−) signs to describe the two ____ along a straight line.
e: However, we will use positive (+) and negative (−) signs to describe the two opposite directions along a straight line. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite directions.

q: The motion graphs are of three types: (i) displacement-time graph (s-t graph), (ii) velocity-time graph (v-t graph) and (iii) ____.
e: The motion graphs are of three types: (i) displacement-time graph (s-t graph), (ii) velocity-time graph (v-t graph) and (iii) acceleration-time graph (a-t graph). Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The slope of the s-t graph gives the ____.
e: The slope of the s-t graph gives the constant velocity. Constant velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Of three types of motion graphs, v-t graph is very useful to analyze a ____.
e: Of three types of motion graphs, v-t graph is very useful to analyze a motion. The physics in this sentence is built around motion.

q: The slope of a v-t graph gives the ____ of a body.
e: The slope of a v-t graph gives the acceleration of a body. Acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The area under a v-t graph gives the ____ (or) distance moved by the body.
e: The area under a v-t graph gives the displacement (or) distance moved by the body. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.
